program.headline: The 4-phase intercept-accuracy program — a causal stack; pointing gates everything
program.summary: ⛔ SUPERSEDED (2026-07-24/25) — this 4-phase 'pointing gates everything' program predates the SETTLED conclusions: the dash-only control arms flew (aim is the dominant lever, ADR-0080/0083), Phase A (accel-cap + loft + wedge) is NET-NEGATIVE at correct aim and NOT a do-first lever, Phase B (fov_guidance) is PARKED (the wrong lever), and the terminal-precision phases are NULLs. Read the levers table + big_lever for the current stack. Kept for the causal-reasoning history. Not a menu: each phase only pays off once the one before it lands, and NONE is ratified — all four are ranked hypotheses, each with a pre-registered sim/bench test (full option-by-option detail: decision intercept_accuracy under the pointing stage, §2.1). Sim numbers are UPPER BOUNDS (the sim has no motion-blur model); the Stage-0 bench confirms. First kills fly the AprilTag — some levers are markerless-only.

phases.name: POINTING
phases.status: GAZEBO A/B DONE — pointing CONFIRMED (recall 3%→35%, centered) but miss WORSE at 9 m/s (closing-speed cost); camera-DRIVEN unconfirmed
phases.what: Accel-capped constant-pitch dash (PRIMARY) + loft-then-dive (complement) + MODEST wedge (~10-15°). Gazebo (n=8 paired): 8-12 m real recall 3.0%→35.4%, in-camera elevation −25.7°→−3.6° (centered), <5 m recall 25%→82% — the pointing wall comes down. BUT the cap slows the run-in (handoff 4.7→3.0 m/s) so miss got WORSE at 9 m/s (0.75→2.93 m). Necessary, not sufficient. Audit a/b clean; camera-driven-ness UNCONFIRMED (check c weak, no dash-only control).
phases.test: SETTLED: analytical (inframe_ab.py) + Gazebo A/B (loft_dive/gazebo_results.md) FLEW. Verdict: framing (loft+wedge) is NET-NEGATIVE at correct aim (CG 1.92 > level 1.32); the accel cap costs closing speed (EAL); dash-only controls settled that AIM, not framing, is the lever. NOT a do-first lever.

phases.name: FOV-HOLD GUIDANCE
phases.what: Look-angle-constrained PN + IBVS pixel-centering: absorbs the +40°→−35° pitch swing the static wedge cannot track, working in pixel space — no noisy bearing differentiation (the thing that sank APN/PIP). Blind if the target is already out of frame — hence gated on A.
phases.test: PARKED — Phase B FOV-hold (flight/fov_guidance.py) was the wrong lever; framing at correct aim hurts, so there is no framing benefit to convert. flight/fov_guidance.py stays parked.

phases.name: SIZE-RANGE FUSION
phases.what: Fuse the monocular size-based range prior (R = fx·W/w_px from the bbox already computed) into the existing range channel to sharpen t_go — which squares into the ~96%-of-miss ZEM budget. Cheapest software lever; NOT a resolution lever.
phases.test: guidance_lab A/B (n≥8): size-R prior vs geometry-only with W-foreshortening injected as noise; measure miss + t_go error.

phases.name: TERMINAL IMU-COAST
phases.status: PRE-CODED + tested (flight/terminal_coast.py) — pays off after A
phases.what: At the sub-1 m camera blackout (camera dies inside ~1 m on 20/20 flights; terminal LOS 485-1870°/s), freeze the last good LOS-rate and fly the final ~0.15 s on the own-state EKF, armed by a tau (time-to-contact) clock — carries the commanded correction through impact.

architecture.summary: ONE NN, THE WHOLE FLIGHT: the detector runs on EVERY camera frame — there is no learned tracker (detect-then-track, NN acquire + CSRT follow, was TRIED and DROPPED: every tracker slips on the banking quad, NN-only won the paired A/B, ADR-0076 add #2). The 'tracking' that flies the intercept is PHYSICS — an alpha-beta filter plus proportional navigation — not a second network. Flight shape: coded open-loop dash (no datalink) -> 5-consecutive-detection streak hands off -> the closed loop below runs every frame to contact.

steps.name: NN, every frame
steps.role: Markerless YOLO drone_finetuned_quad_v2 @640 (conf 0.25) finds the target box in each camera frame; the AprilTag is only the staged first-kill baseline, never the markerless seeker's input.

steps.name: box -> bearing + range
steps.role: Box centre + camera intrinsics (Brown-Conrady undistort) -> bearing; calibrated box WIDTH -> range.

steps.name: physics filter
steps.role: Full-attitude LOS derotation (FIX-A) + fixed-gain alpha-beta filters on angle/range: predict at 20 Hz, correct on each fresh detection (~14 Hz stream), coast through dropouts. PHYSICS, not a learned tracker.

steps.name: pro-nav, N=5
steps.role: Lateral accel = N x closing-speed x LOS-rate — the classic missile law; pursuit kept in-tree as the A/B baseline.

steps.name: MAVSDK setpoint
steps.role: Accel command -> velocity/attitude setpoint to PX4 OFFBOARD (the portable flight/ core — runs unchanged on the real Pi/Pixhawk).

stages.active: Auto collision-lead heading from pre-flight target kinematics (honest constant, no live gt); --dash-heading-deg override ('human points it').
stages.note: Aim tolerance measured: all 48 flights still acquired/engaged at up to +/-30 deg heading error (weave) — but #18g showed ENGAGE streaks can be phantom, so read that as dash-robustness, not perception proof. Onboard acoustic tracking REJECTED (own-noise ~40 dB the wrong way); acoustics OK only as a future GROUND launch-cue (idea). RELEASE/LAUNCH-MECHANISM options evaluated 2026-07-21 (decision launch_mech, docs/launch_mechanism_options.md): recommend B-core (manual trigger + coded dash) + an honesty-clean launch-time aim stack — a static-camera bearing latch and an OPTIONAL no-radio one-shot ground spotter, both latched as pre-flight constants; autonomous launch-on-detect (auto-fire) and a live-datalink cue are REJECTED (graveyard + constraint no-datalink). The launch choice is largely orthogonal to the binding wall (POINTING); the aim-stack extension is validation-gated on the fixed-tilt re-fly, NOT ratified. | AIM LEVER CONFIRMED 2026-07-24 (G20dash decomposition, n=8 paired dash-only, logs/mc_fp_armG20dash_line9_s123.csv): the crossing-bias aim constant was MIS-SIZED (collision_lead_heading solves a constant-speed triangle but the dash accelerates from rest). Correcting +30°→+20° for the baseline accel drops the OPEN-LOOP dash-only ballistic combined median 1.37→0.75 m, 7/8 paired better (l2r 2.05→0.73 the big win; r2l already near-optimal) — meets the pre-registered CONFIRM (≥6/8 AND median ≤0.90). A free, honest, pre-flight lever (launch-time constant, no gt/cue) = the cheapest miss-reduction found for the coded dash. HONEST: 0.75 m is the dash-only floor (camera off); the point-mass model over-predicted 0.14 m (ranked the aim right, absolute wrong). Real build implication: the collision-lead constant must be sized for the ACCELERATING dash, not constant-speed — a code fix that carries to hardware. Next: G20 (camera-live bias 20) tests if the terminal improves on 0.75 m at correct aim. | ADR-0080 SIM-VALIDATED 2026-07-24 (accel-aware lead auto-derives the aim): AAL dash-only reproduces the hand-tuned +20 on seed 123 (0.71 vs 0.75, 6/8 within 0.2 m) AND GENERALIZES to disjoint seed 777 (0.57 m, tighter; auto-derived +21.3°, honesty-clean pre-flight constants only). The crossing-bias is now a DERIVED kinematic constant, not a per-config knob — removes the aim-tuning burden from the real build. | ⭐ AIM OPTIMUM NOT YET REACHED (2026-07-24): the dash-only aim curve measures 0° 0.71 m → +5° 0.43 m → +15° 1.43 m (same seeds, paired), so ADR-0080's derived lead sits ~5° off a real optimum worth ~0.28 m. Load-bearing because the honest 5-inch ram envelope is 0.35 m (ADR-0084): a 0.43 m open-loop dash is knocking on it, 0.71 m is not. AIM REFINEMENT — not the camera — is the only measured path into the kill envelope, and it costs pre-flight arithmetic. AE2/AE7/AE10 bracketing arms staged to DERIVE the optimum into the solver rather than leave a hand-found offset. | ADR-0083 ADOPTED 2026-07-24: a +5.0° EMPIRICAL aim trim (--dash-aim-trim-deg, default off) takes the open-loop dash-only miss 0.71 → ~0.43 m pooled (14/16 paired, p=0.0021, seeds 123+777; r2l cell 0.33 m = INSIDE the ~0.36 m ram envelope). MEASURED, NOT DERIVED — the mechanism hunt found a real defect (solver a=10 vs measured pre-CPA ~3.1 m/s²; 22.2 m predicted travel by CPA vs 8.2 m actual) but substituting it swings the heading 30-70° against a ~5° empirical optimum, so it is deliberately NOT baked into the solver. Per-config constant: MUST be re-measured on the real airframe from the first dash ULog.

constraints.text: Pi 5 CPU runs the AprilTag baseline seeker real-time; markerless YOLO REQUIRES the (deferred) Hailo AI HAT+ — CPU YOLO ~5-10 FPS is not viable at terminal LOS rates. First real kills therefore fly the tag.

Pi 5 performance CANNOT be pre-validated in emulation: a QEMU/ARM64 VM proves the SOFTWARE stack (ONNX loads, the pipeline runs end-to-end) but NOT real fps — emulated throughput is not representative of real Cortex-A76 performance. Real numbers need the physical Pi 5 (the Tier-1 buy, bom_tiers) or the Hailo vendor benchmark. Anchors: AprilTag ~30 fps CPU-real-time; markerless YOLO ~5-10 fps CPU (measured ~13 fps YOLOv8n on desktop-class CPU, ADR-0015) — not viable at terminal LOS rates, REQUIRES the Hailo HAT.
The ~100 deg wide FoV is a HARD requirement, not a tunable — the +/-30 deg open-loop aim tolerance depends on it. Never fit/fly a narrow lens.

The own-prop phantom has NO software fallback (phantom-free retrain fails blind in flight; every gate NULL). Prop clearance must be designed in by geometry (nose-cantilever mount) and verified by the bench corner-spin check — a HARD gate.
No guidance datalink (the jam-resistance story): the dash is open-loop, ELRS is kill/arm only, SiK is telemetry-monitoring only. Nothing mid-course steers the interceptor except its own camera.

gt_* is scoring/logging ONLY; guidance sees camera + own-state EKF only. AprilTag is sanctioned for calibration, training-time auto-labels, and the staged baseline seeker — never as an input to the deployed markerless seeker.

The MIT-licensed outdoor-drone-NN transfer bet is UNVALIDATED (hope past evidence). Cheapest kill-or-validate: the ~$310 tripod + tagged-target afternoon measuring real approach-recall vs range/frame-position. Its verdict gates ONLY the Hailo HAT + the markerless phase — the interceptor order is gated on the SAME session's AprilTag envelope curve instead (first kills fly the tag, §0c), so a dead transfer bet delays markerless, not the build. [SMOKE READ 2026-07-21, P0.6 — docs/transfer_bet_kill_test.md: NOT DEAD (quad_v2 boxes a real DJI 2/3 clean photos — the sim->real generalization exists) but NOT alive-and-well (raw per-frame discrimination ~zero: 0.71 drone-frames vs 0.65 drone-FREE — clutter fires); the deciding variable is the 5-streak handoff gate on real clutter, which only tripod curve (b) can measure.]

FIVE mirages were caught in the coded-dash arc alone (rebal 16/16, camera-guided r2l, resolution probe, up35 capture, static-aspect wall). Any new 'win' needs a control arm (dash-only / gt-consistent audit), paired seeds n>=8, and validation on held-out FLIGHTS — never frame-eval or single-seed.
Success criterion is a BINARY KILL confirmed on video + both ULogs; a citable sub-meter CPA number is explicitly NOT required (RTK cut — buy later only for a portfolio number).

MOUNT RISK CHECKLIST — five checks before the committed nose-cantilever mount flies (Fable gap-check 2026-07-17, biggest-bite first): (1) TILT/CLEARANCE COLLISION: the mount clears the props by only ~11° at LEVEL (§0②), and the chosen fixed up-tilt (~dash pitch, 25-40°) far exceeds that — tilting rotates the FoV edge toward the prop disc; verify clearance AT the chosen tilt under LOADED throttle (not idle+level), and the bench-verified angle CAPS the printable tilt. (2) Boom VIBRATION: tip flex (bending mode plausibly in the 40-150 Hz prop band) injects bearing noise AFTER derotation (~17-35 mrad per +-1-2 deg, same order as the ADR-0056 aspect bias) + motion blur on the recall wall -> the mount can undercut its own benefit; fix by STIFFNESS (short, gusseted, carbon insert), NOT a soft-mount (which trades blur for worse low-freq extrinsic wobble). (3) LEVER-ARM: the camera is forward of the CG/IMU -> a real terminal LOS parallax; the sim harness compensates (m4:2493, honest 3-D) but the portable flight/ core NOW carries it (flight.geometry.camera_to_cg_los, tested) — the real terminal must CALL it with the mount constant; and LINK the offset flag to the model swap so it can't silently fly uncompensated. (4) The camera LEADS the contact kill -> sacrificial each shot (BOM spares line + breakaway boom). (5) CSI-2 ribbon on a vibrating boom -> flex-fatigue/EMI frame-drops that MIMIC detection dropouts; log camera frame-arrival rate SEPARATELY from detection rate. NOT a factor: forward CG does NOT change the dash pitch (pitch attitude = atan(a/g), commanded-accel-set, not CG).
evidence: Fable gap-check 2026-07-17 (verified: ~11 deg level margin in §0②; flight/ lever-arm since fixed; m4:2493 sim compensation is honest)

graveyard.why: Own-prop noise ~40 dB the wrong way. (Ground launch-cue variant stays an idea.)

graveyard.what: Bank-as-accel predictive cue / APN augmentation (read target bank -> feed-forward a_lat)
graveyard.why: MEASURED DEAD 2026-07-21 (pre-code feasibility gate on the real quad_dataset_banked): under the terminal ~23 px motion smear (which spans the whole 8-15 px target) bank-SNR collapses to ~1-2 and sigma_a = 6-12 m/s^2 -- LARGER than the ~4.7 m/s^2 jink signal it would feed forward, so it injects more error than signal. Independently: on the STRAIGHT-LINE mission target the APN augmentation term is identically zero (== plain PN), so it buys nothing on the actual mission. Reading bank off a few-px blurred silhouette is optically implausible, as predicted (ADR-0073). Do not build it as guidance; the tool experiments/darkhorse/bank_feasibility.py stays as the audit.

graveyard.what: Live mid-course datalink cue from a 'smart launcher' (Option C as-stated)
graveyard.why: REJECTED as-stated: a persistent launcher->interceptor cue VIOLATES the no-datalink jam-resistance constraint (it IS the link an adversary jams) and was MEASURED to hurt aim (cue-guided r2l 0/8 vs coded-dash 5/8 @Pk2.5, aspect-biased bearing). Survives ONLY recast as a zero-radio ONE-SHOT pre-launch spotter that latches a single pre-flight constant and lets the link die at launch. Do not add a live guidance datalink.

graveyard.what: Autonomous launch-on-detect (auto-fire a spinning-prop ram on an NN lock)
graveyard.why: REJECTED as a standalone/auto-fire path: zero added acquisition range + reaction-time-starved (~1.8 s vs 9 m/s inbound), does not touch the pointing wall, and auto-firing a RAM on an unmeasured outdoor false-positive rate (ADR-0078 bird/clutter) is the least-defensible ROE. The salvageable half — latching the reliable STATIC camera bearing as a pre-flight-constant launch heading — is kept, but the human keeps the fire decision.

graveyard.what: Porpoise / pitch-up re-framing pulses during the dash
graveyard.why: REJECTED (intercept-accuracy vetting 2026-07-21): strictly dominated by loft-then-dive (which gives CONTINUOUS framing for free) and it manufactures the exact +40->-35 attitude swing the project is trying to escape, adding self-induced body-rate blur at the worst moment while each 0.2-0.3 s relaxation spends ~25-33% of the terminal engagement decelerating.

REJECTED (2026-07-21): an impact-angle constraint provably EATS lateral-accel authority, degrading the ZEM-nulling that sets 96% of the miss, while the cross-section gain for two sub-0.3 m bodies is unproven and small. Salvageable kernel (bias EARLY toward near-head-on to lower terminal LOS rate + aid framing) is a different, weaker idea.

graveyard.what: Early FOV-bounded observability weave (bearings-only range excitation)
graveyard.why: REJECTED as a headline lever (2026-07-21): real bearings-only physics, but it spends the SCARCEST resource -- pointing/FOV margin -- to buy a range the straight-line target barely needs (plain PN nulls lambda_dot without explicit range); likely net-negative vs the pointing wall, gain probably below the ~1 m terminal-dropout noise floor.

graveyard.what: Auto-crop / foveated-crop (resolution) as the acquisition lever
graveyard.why: TESTED AND REJECTED: crop gives IDENTICAL recall to full-frame at the 8-12 m wall band (33%/33%, 0%/0%) — the earlier '47->71% crop win' was edge-clipped <=6 m targets (3rd mirage). Resolution matters only past ~24 m static, irrelevant to the wall. Do not build crops or buy sensors for range.
Both NULL: ace frame-eval, fail in flight (v3 regressed all 10 held-out flights; rebal flies blind, 0/16 acquisitions). Do not resurrect.

ADR-0077 gate regressed l2r 81%->25% (a phantom-seeded r_hat makes the gate reject the TRUE closing detections); --coded-dash-acquire-range-* aborted both directions — because approach recall ~0 (nothing real to acquire, add #18g corrected the earlier 'ranges overlap' mechanism). decisions.question: Which terminal guidance law drives the camera-only intercept — pursuit, plain proportional navigation, PIP lead, accel-predictive APN, or Kalata-gain tracking?

options.name: Pursuit (steer at current target position)
options.summary: Command velocity straight at where the target is right now. The simplest possible law; kept in the tree as the permanent A/B baseline.
options.why_choose: You would pick pursuit if you wanted zero target-state estimation: it needs only the current bearing, has no filter states to tune, and cannot be poisoned by a bad velocity estimate. It is also the honest control arm — pro-nav's value is only demonstrable against it.
options.pros: Trivial to implement and debug; maximally robust to measurement noise (uses no derivatives); its failure IS the resume finding (the M4 comparison).
options.cons: Structurally laggy against any crossing target — it flies a tail-chase. M4 gate: pursuit 2.05–2.54 m vs pro-nav 0.28–0.44 m on identical paths (4.6–7.6x worse at 2 m/s). Its expected endgame failure is spinning off-boresight and losing the tag.

options.name: Plain proportional navigation (a = N*Vc*lambda_dot, N=5)
options.summary: Command lateral acceleration proportional to the line-of-sight rotation rate, mechanized strapdown (lambda = psi + beta) with alpha-beta filters and full-attitude LOS derotation (FIX-A). The deployed law, now extracted into the portable flight/ core.
options.why_choose: Pick pro-nav because it is feedback on the LOS *rate* only — it needs no target position/velocity/acceleration track — so it survives the noisy, intermittent ~14 Hz monocular stream that broke every lead law. It won M4 decisively (4.6–7.6x over pursuit at 2 m/s), and the adopted config later hardened to Pk >= 95% (95% CI, n=72) at a 2.8 m proximity radius (ADR-0064, billboard target).
options.pros: Sensor-light and robust to dropouts; the classic missile law (the resume line); bounded miss growth under maneuver; validated across the whole M0–M5 arc and unchanged into the coded-dash real-build architecture.
options.cons: By design leaves nonzero miss against a maneuvering target; at FPV crossing speed it TIES pursuit because kinematics (delivered ZEM at handoff) dominate the law (ADR-0029/0036 regime map); the ~1.5–2 m weave CPA is the practical floor of this seeker architecture (ADR-0070/0071).

options.name: PIP (Predicted Intercept Point lead law)
options.summary: Solve the intercept triangle (quadratic) on a target position+velocity track and fly to the predicted point. Won the clean-sensor lab 2–4x on all 7 paths; kept as --law pip, default-off.
options.why_choose: PIP is the genuine cure for 'lagging behind a fast crosser' — it predicts where the target will be instead of reacting to LOS rotation. It is the right law wherever a CLEAN velocity track exists: it won the two-stage dash config in the recalibrated lab, and the dash phase's collision-lead solve is exactly this machinery fed by the cue (legal, pre-handoff).
options.pros: True prediction; theoretically superior; the dash-phase lead solve descends from it.
options.cons: Its lead point is only as good as the target-velocity estimate. Gazebo's real monocular stream (bearing/range noise + 30–40% dropouts) starved the alpha-beta velocity track: PIP flew 3.03 m vs pure PN's 1.6 m at a 4 m/s crosser (ADR-0011 addendum), and only tied PN in the S2 gate. A resume-worthy negative: the theoretically superior law degraded under realistic sensor noise.

options.name: APN / accel-predictive (Kalman-CA, OGL-ZEM, PIP-with-accel)
options.summary: Augment PN with an estimated target acceleration term (a = N*Vc*lambda_dot + (N/2)*a_T) — the textbook maneuvering-target upgrade. Assessed twice, rejected twice.
options.why_choose: You would build APN if the maneuver term dominated the miss and you had a clean acceleration signal: it is the industry-standard answer to a weaving target (Zarchan), and the builder explicitly asked for it ('2 m is too much — predict from acceleration').
options.pros: Formally optimal against constant-accel maneuvers; the industry standard the portfolio should be able to discuss.
options.cons: Two hard walls. (1) Noise: acceleration from a monocular track needs a 2nd derivative — measured sigma_a ~7 m/s^2 vs a 4.71 m/s^2 weave signal, SNR < 1 (ADR-0069 kill-gate). (2) It attacks the wrong term: the miss decomposition shows ~84% (~1.6 m) of the 12 m/s weave miss is the fast-crossing kinematic floor present even at zero target accel; the maneuver term is only ~0.27 m. Even a clean-bearing AprilTag floors at 1.64 m (ADR-0056). The one live re-open path is the bank-as-accel cue (ADR-0073: tan(bank)=a_lat/g, no differentiation), feasibility-gated and unbuilt.

options.name: Kalata tracking-index gains
options.summary: Compute the alpha-beta filter gains from the actual measurement dt each correction (Kalata 1984) instead of fixed gains — principled dropout handling for free. Won the lab by 24–28%; rejected in Gazebo.
options.why_choose: Pick Kalata if the measurement cadence were smooth: it is the principled way to make a fixed-gain filter dt-aware, and it beat fixed-gain pure PN in 19/21 lab cells.
options.pros: Theoretically sound; free dropout response; a clean, citable estimation-theory result either way.
options.cons: Gazebo's real cadence is BIMODAL (~14 Hz bursts plus multi-second handoff gaps) and the lab-tuned sigmas go degenerate at both extremes — every Kalata-enabled flight was worse (3.24 m vs the 1.09–2.25 m no-flag cluster), with the mechanism caught directly in the logged effective gains (ADR-0013). The third data point in the 'lab ranks, Gazebo decides' meta-lesson.

decisions.chosen_rationale: Plain pro-nav won because every theoretically-superior alternative (PIP, APN, Kalata) depends on estimating target state from a noisy, intermittent monocular stream, and each one measurably degraded in Gazebo where PN — needing only the LOS rate — held. The project's regime map completes the picture: the guidance LAW dominates at low speed (M4's 4.6–7.6x win), washes out at FPV speed where engagement geometry (running start / coded dash) and kill radius are the real levers (ADR-0029/0036), and the residual ~1.5–2 m weave CPA is a seeker bearing-quality + kinematic floor no law tightens (ADR-0069/0070/0071) — which is already a proximity-fuse kill under the ratified metric. The law and architecture remain validated (billboard 72/72, ADR-0064); note honestly that the camera-guided terminal kill of the 3D quad is NOT yet validated — that block is upstream in the detector/pointing, not the guidance (ADR-0076 add #18h).

decisions.question: Which target-state estimator feeds the guidance — the hand-set alpha-beta filter stack, or a covariance-weighted EKF?

options.name: Alpha-beta (g-h) filters + hand-set polar FusedTrack
options.summary: Fixed-gain alpha-beta filters on lambda and range (predict 20 Hz, correct on fresh detections), with the mid-course cue fused by a hand-set polar rule (cue never touches the angle). The deployed tracker.
options.why_choose: Pick alpha-beta because the miss is kinematically capped, so a better filter cannot move it — and because fixed weights proved MORE robust than live covariance weighting: the hand-set polar FusedTrack survived the WORST-tier 2.5 m datum-bias cue 8/8 clean where the EKF's chi-square gate locked onto the bias and rejected the true camera (ADR-0044).
options.pros: Simple, tuned, validated everywhere; structurally immune to the gate-rejects-the-truth failure class (no camera gate exists); the polar split keeps cue bias out of the bearing channel by construction.
options.cons: Cannot weight sources by live uncertainty; fixed gains are cadence-sensitive (the Kalata lesson); velocity estimates from position-only streams are poor (why the cue emits velocity).

options.name: Cartesian-CV EKF (--tracker ekf) with covariance-gated fusion
options.summary: A proper extended Kalman filter with innovation (chi-square) gating and covariance weighting — the 'textbook right' estimator and the most-asked GNC interview topic. Built, instrumented, A/B'd, kept default-off.
options.why_choose: Pick the EKF if source quality varies live: covariance weighting natively de-weights a degrading cue and the innovation gate natively rejects a wrong measurement — adaptive fusion falls out of the estimator instead of hand-coded if-statements (ADR-0034). It also produced the project's tightest-ever markerless misses (0.151/0.229 m) on flights with deep terminal custody.
options.pros: Principled uncertainty handling; elegant fallback semantics; a sophisticated portfolio answer even as a null.
options.cons: The pre-registered A/B was NULL on miss AND track RMSE, and the paired clean-rate exposed a terminal-hold regression at the shipped Q (ADR-0037; later re-scored to parity under abort-lens correction). Decisively: under the WORST-tier biased cue the tuned chi-square gate rejects 81–100% of VALID camera corrections (confident-bias-lock) — the survival check FAILED 5/8 with a 7.66 m flyby vs the hand-set's 8/8 (ADR-0041/0044). Fatter bad tail; complexity not earned.

decisions.chosen_rationale: Alpha-beta stays for measured reasons, not simplicity-bias: the miss is kinematically capped so estimator quality doesn't reach it (ADR-0023/0037), and when it mattered most — a biased/spoofed cue — the fixed-weight polar discipline beat live covariance weighting outright (ADR-0044: 8/8 WORST survival vs 5/8 with a flyby). The T20 refinement design (range-agreement monitor, ADR-0054) was then honestly pre-registered-NULLed when the T17-v2 retrain removed the bias it targeted (ADR-0055). The EKF machinery stays in-tree, fully instrumented, as the documented negative result.

decisions.question: What does the terminal seeker lock on — a markerless neural-net detector, the AprilTag fiducial, an IR/thermal seeker, or classical motion CV?

options.name: Markerless NN seeker (fine-tuned YOLO)
options.summary: A single-class fine-tuned YOLO detector reading raw camera pixels — the deployed seeker (drone_finetuned_quad_v2 @640, conf 0.25). Builder-ratified as the thing that must fly: 'it is imperative we make markerless work'.
options.why_choose: This is the project's thesis: a real hostile drone carries no fiducial, so killing the AprilTag is what converts the work from 'guidance demo with a solved perception problem' into genuine seeker development. It was sim-validated against the billboard target (detect-then-track 14/14 post-handoff at 12 m/s weave, zero phantom handoffs, ADR-0058), the tag->NN swap re-earned the full no-cheat audit, and the identical stack transfers to the Pi 5 + Hailo flight computer (ADR-0063).
options.pros: Deployable honesty; one stack from sim to real; measured (not assumed) costs vs the tag; in a fast CROSSING dash it actually beats the tag (the directional tag goes invisible — ADR-0076 add #18e).
options.cons: Measured regression vs the tag: +1 m median miss and ~25 pp clean-rate, driven by sparse detection (ADR-0038); box-center bearing noise is the binding terminal quality limit (ADR-0056). The current wall: in-flight approach recall on the 3D quad is 0.8% >= 8 m even though static/centred recall is 100% at 8–22 m — a FLIGHT-DYNAMIC pointing/attitude deficit, not appearance or resolution (ADR-0076 add #18k). Real-time on hardware REQUIRES the deferred Hailo HAT.

options.name: AprilTag fiducial seeker
options.summary: The sanctioned sim stand-in for 'a reliable target lock exists' — sub-degree subpixel-corner bearing, ~5% range, CPU-real-time. Now scoped to calibration, training-time auto-labels, and the staged first-kill baseline seeker.
options.why_choose: Pick the tag when you need to isolate guidance from perception (its original GOALS.md role), when compute is scarce (Pi 5 CPU runs it real-time, so the first real kills fly the tag while the Hailo HAT is deferred), or as measurement infrastructure (the tag pose auto-labels real footage for the markerless retrain, and it is the perception ceiling every markerless result is scored against — the clean-bearing control that held 8/8 at 1.64 m through the 12 m/s weave, ADR-0056).
options.pros: Clean, robust, cheap; the honest control arm; CPU-real-time; the calibration/labeling backbone of the real-data pipeline.
options.cons: No real threat carries one — a headline built on it flatters (the billboard/tag era's 72/72 vs the quad's ~41% is the cautionary tale); the directional ~6 m tag is INVISIBLE during a 16 m/s crossing dash (0 detections, ADR-0076 add #18e), so it is not even a viable terminal seeker in the crossing regime; it must never feed the deployed markerless seeker (honesty boundary).

options.name: IR / thermal seeker
options.summary: A thermal camera as the terminal lock channel — the fielded C-UAS night answer (Ukrainian thermal FPV interceptors).
options.why_choose: You would pick IR for night/low-contrast operation or if target-vs-sky contrast were the failure mode — it is what capability-first fielded systems add, and it was explicitly offered by the builder ('IR if needed').
options.pros: Night capability; robust contrast against sky; validated by fielded systems.
options.cons: A non-sequitur for this project's measured bottleneck: the council found the lock failure is geometric/kinematic, not sensing-modality (ADR-0014 cut it as dishonest/ineffective spend), and ADR-0022's lever ranking rejected it again as costly/ineffective. Thermal roughly doubles cost, is blind at thermal crossover (dawn/dusk), and the staged-thermal ruling that survives is for the GROUND rig night channel (ADR-0019), not the onboard seeker.

options.name: Classical frame-differencing CV
options.summary: Motion-proposal classical CV (the parent design's original Pi-Zero seeker) — no training, near-zero compute.
options.why_choose: You would pick classical CV for its compute economics: it runs on a $18 board and needs no dataset or training pipeline at all.
options.pros: Trivial compute; no ML toolchain; no license questions.
options.cons: Empirically dead in this repo: the built prototype's 40/40 'detections' were own-airframe edge wedges at confidence 1.0 — a standing high-confidence FALSE bearing (seeker_prototype_results.md). It has no identity channel, so it cannot do the cue-validated seed or IoU re-validation that fixed the maneuver phantom, and its ego-motion compensation structurally degrades under the measured 42–52 deg nose-down dash where terrain, not sky, is behind the target. Rejected 3/3 by the flight-compute council (ADR-0063).

decisions.chosen_rationale: Markerless is chosen because it IS the capability being claimed — the builder ratified it verbatim over the council dissent's staged-tag path, and the dissent's substance was kept (bench gate before airframe money, tag arc as the documented fallback). The 2026-07-15/16 re-scope sharpens the division of labor rather than reversing it: the AprilTag remains load-bearing as calibration + auto-labeler + the staged first-kill baseline (Pi 5 CPU real-time), while the markerless seeker is the end-state whose one make-or-break unknown is now precisely localized — flight-dynamic pointing/attitude recall, not static appearance (ADR-0076 add #18k). IR and classical CV both fail the measured-bottleneck test.
decisions.evidence: ADR-0014, ADR-0019, ADR-0022, ADR-0038, ADR-0056, ADR-0058, ADR-0063, ADR-0076 add #18e/#18h/#18k, docs/real_data_pipeline.md, hardware_order_list.md §0c

decisions.question: Which trained detector weights fly — v2, the v3 maneuvering-domain retrain, the rebal phantom-free retrain, or a real-data retrain?

options.name: v2 (drone_finetuned_quad_v2.onnx @640, conf 0.25)
options.summary: The deployed weights: the quad-target fine-tune descended from the v2 recipe (hard negatives + range calibration, ADR-0042). The only weights with real in-flight intercepts on the 3D quad (l2r 81–88%).
options.why_choose: Keep v2 because it is the only detector that actually works in flight, and both challengers regressed there while acing their own offline evals. Its lineage carries the validated mechanism fixes: pollution 0.751 -> 0.000, range calibration 0.056 -> 0.935, audit-clean (ADR-0042).
options.pros: Real flight-validated intercepts; calibrated range; zero near-boresight pollution; the honest baseline every experiment is paired against.
options.cons: In-flight approach recall 0.8% >= 8 m on the quad (the wall — though now known to be flight-dynamic pointing, not v2's appearance model); a residual r2l aspect bias (ADR-0056 class); static acquisition ceiling ~24 m.

options.name: v3 maneuvering-domain retrain
options.summary: The ADR-0053/0055 ground-detector medicine (train the deployment domain, structural split, held-out eval) applied to the onboard detector's 12 m/s weave/jink domain: 648-pose static grid + 16 ride-along flights.
options.why_choose: The case for v3 was strong on paper: the identical recipe demonstrably FIXED the ground detector's out-of-domain bias (ADR-0055, held-out-validated), and the onboard detector's far-range flight recall (0.47) was the named weak link.
options.pros: Methodologically sound dataset (leakage-audited two independent ways, so the null is real); the correct instinct — train the domain you deploy in.
options.cons: NULL / mild regression: v3 regressed flight recall on ALL 10 held-out flights (0.47->0.19 maneuver, 0.59->0.18 line, paired sign p=0.002) while acing its own static-grid val — static far-range data did NOT transfer to the flight far-range problem. Its lower phantom rate was a side-effect of firing 5–20x less. A pre-results forward audit + 4 pre-registered scorer fixes prevented a false win (ADR-0061). Closed; do NOT resurrect.

options.name: rebal / hardened negative-mining retrain
options.summary: Balance-corrected retrains that suppress the own-prop phantom (565–1436 mined hard negatives).
options.why_choose: The case: the phantom was believed to be the r2l blocker and the false-handoff trigger, and phantom-vs-target are co-located but appearance-separable — so appearance retraining looked like the correct discriminator (ADR-0076 add #10). The mining even succeeded at its literal goal: phantom suppressed, real target acquired ~13 m earlier (add #11).
options.pros: Did kill the phantom; proved by elimination that the phantom was NOT the r2l cause — a diagnostic win.
options.cons: Flies blind: rebal coverage 0.000–0.019 across all 16 coded-dash flights, every one aborting 'no camera acquire' — its tempting '16/16 Pk' was open-loop dash ballistics, not vision (ADR-0076 add #18d); the hardened variant regressed l2r 88%->0 (under-training) and left r2l unchanged. The same aced-frame-eval / failed-in-flight trap as v3, one level up. Closed NULLs.

options.name: Real-data retrain (COCO-init + AprilTag auto-labels)
options.summary: Retrain on real captured footage: autolabel_from_apriltag.py (tag pose -> YOLO labels), COCO-init never sim weights, ~15–20% negatives, validate on held-out FLIGHTS. Pipeline built and Fable-hardened; not yet run.
options.why_choose: This is the only path to the OUTDOOR appearance gap — sim pixels cannot teach real optics, backgrounds, and lighting. The recipe encodes every hard-won anti-mirage rule (flight-level validation, negatives policy, tag-miss frames dropped).
options.pros: Attacks the one gap sim structurally cannot close; the labeling trick is honesty-clean (tag used offline at training time only).
options.cons: DEMOTED from critical-path-certain to HYPOTHESIS for the sim wall (ADR-0076 add #18k): a static/hover capture would ace static tests and still fail in flight — the v3/rebal trap again. Any capture MUST include approaching passes at speed, off-boresight/frame-edge placements, and banked attitudes, scored vs position-in-frame. The MIT outdoor-NN transfer bet is UNVALIDATED — kill-or-validate with the ~$310 tripod + tagged-target afternoon BEFORE building.

decisions.chosen_rationale: v2 stays deployed because it is the only detector with in-flight results, and the project's sharpest recurring lesson is that offline/frame-eval gains repeatedly fail in flight (v3, rebal, and the ground v1's necessary-not-sufficient PASS all demonstrate it). That lesson is now codified: any new detector claim needs held-out FLIGHTS, control arms, and paired seeds — never frame-eval or a single geometry. The real-data retrain remains the live future lever, but for the outdoor gap, not the sim wall, and only after the cheap tripod validation of the transfer bet.
decisions.evidence: ADR-0042, ADR-0061, ADR-0076 add #18d/#18k, docs/real_data_pipeline.md, project_state.json graveyard

decisions.question: How is the terminal lock held frame-to-frame — detect-then-track (NN seed + CSRT follow), NN-only, or a learned ViT tracker?

options.name: Detect-then-track (--track: NN acquires once, cv2 CSRT follows, NN re-validates every 8 frames)
options.summary: The builder-insight architecture that fixed the billboard-era maneuvering false-lock: temporal consistency filters phantoms that no confidence gate can (confidence is INVERTED — phantom 0.34 > real 0.17).
options.why_choose: Pick detect-then-track against a RIGID-appearance target: it recovered weave 3/16 -> 14/14 post-handoff and jink 3/15 -> 14/15 with phantom handoffs 12 -> 0 (ADR-0058), and its jink win proved the value is temporal DENSITY, not only phantom rejection. It is also the architecture the flight-compute decision (ADR-0063) was ratified around.
options.pros: Denser than the ~14 Hz NN; ignores phantom boxes elsewhere in frame; the validated billboard-era deployment config; honesty-hardened (cue only pre-handoff, AST-pinned).
options.cons: A correlation/appearance tracker cannot hold a BANKING quad — appearance changes every frame, CSRT loses and re-seeds ~25x/flight, the flickering lock forms the handoff streak too late (ADR-0076 addendum #1), and on the canonical geometry --track degraded even the clean l2r bearing (add #8).

options.name: NN-only (drop --track)
options.summary: Feed the guidance directly from raw NN detections through the alpha-beta filters — no visual tracker. The deployed config for the 3D quad target.
options.why_choose: Pick NN-only when the target's appearance churns (banking quad): every tracker tested slips the lock, so the tracked bearing is WORSE than the NN's own detections — the paired A/B read CSRT 1/8, NN-only 4/8, revalidate-2/4 0/8, ViT 0/8 (ADR-0076 addendum #2).
options.pros: Best measured Pk on the maneuvering quad; one less subsystem; the alpha-beta filter already smooths per-frame jitter.
options.cons: Capped by the NN's own detection coverage (~50% on the quad — no tracker can exceed it, but none can help either); more exposed to a transient phantom at the handoff moment (why handoff hardening is planned).

options.name: Learned ViT tracker
options.summary: An appearance-robust learned tracker swapped in for CSRT, hypothesized to survive the banking-quad appearance churn.
options.why_choose: The principled next step once CSRT's correlation model was diagnosed as the failure: a learned embedding should tolerate appearance change better than raw correlation.
options.pros: Integrated and available as a committed option; may help a less-aggressive target.
options.cons: 0/8 on the paired quad A/B — the banking quad slips this lock too. Shelved.

decisions.chosen_rationale: The tracker verdict is TARGET-DEPENDENT, and both results stand in their own scope: detect-then-track is the validated fix for a rigid-appearance target (the ADR-0058 numbers are real and mechanism-proven), but a hard-banking 3D quad defeats every tracker tried, so the quad's deployed config is NN-only. The interim '--track fixes r2l' claim was retracted when the canonical geometry contradicted the easier 30 m capture geometry (add #7 -> #8) — the incident that produced the standing reproduce-the-canonical-geometry methodology rule.

decisions.question: How does the camera point through the nose-down dash — fixed level (no tilt), a fixed up-tilt mount, or adaptive/active tilt?

options.name: Fixed level forward camera (no tilt)
options.summary: Boresight = body forward, zero mount angle. The current deployed configuration — every validated number was flown on it.
options.why_choose: Keep level because nothing else has earned adoption: it is the simplest mount, all guidance math and gates are validated on it, and both tilt alternatives measurably failed their adoption bars. On hardware it is zero weight, zero moving parts.
options.pros: Simplicity; the validated baseline; no derotation composition needed.
options.cons: The dash pitches 27–52 deg nose-down, throwing the horizon-level target to the frame TOP: ~35% of dash ticks it is entirely above the FoV, and first in-range detection threads a 0–6 deg sliver with ~zero vertical margin (ADR-0060). This is now measured as the DOMINANT cause of the in-flight recall wall — the target sits ~+41 deg off-axis at 11 m, where training never showed it (ADR-0076 add #18k). The sim UNDER-states the gap for real drag-limited hardware. [2026-07-17] Rejected: leaves the acquisition-band target above the frame top during the dash (exits >~11 m); the binding wall.

options.name: Fixed up-tilt mount (angle = measured dash pitch, printed adjustable 10-30°)
options.summary: A fixed wedge canting the camera UP by the airframe's steady DASH PITCH so the boresight tracks the horizon (the crossing target) during the dash. Builder-CHOSEN 2026-07-17; the angle is real-measured (first-dash ULog), never sim-sized — hence the adjustable bracket.
options.why_choose: Simplest possible pointing fix — a printed wedge, no servo/gimbal/power/failure-mode. Sized to the dash pitch it re-centres the acquisition-band target that a level camera loses off the top. Angle = the REAL airframe's measured dash pitch (~25-40°; sim ~35°). NOTE the prior up15 NULL (ADR-0068) was an S2-CUE-era terminal-PARITY test; this is a different context — acquisition-first, under the coded-dash + camera-forward architecture, sized to the dash pitch not a guessed +15.
options.pros: Closes the dash FoV gap; no actuator; trivially cheap.
options.cons: Cannot track the pitch swing (accel->brake), so it trades terminal centring for acquisition; and a dash-pitch-sized tilt exceeds the flush mount's ~11° prop clearance -> forces the boom/elevated-mast mount.

options.name: Adaptive / active camera tilt (#46, ADR-0065)
options.summary: A servo/gimbal that schedules camera pitch against the vehicle's actual pitch: up in the dash, back toward horizon at dash-end. Built (committed 8657320, default-off, own-state-only controller + live derotation); the A/B is the open build.
options.why_choose: Pick adaptive tilt because it is the only pointing scheme that can hold the target through the measured 40-down -> 34-up pitch swing — exactly what dooms any fixed angle — and pointing/attitude is now the DOMINANT lever for the flight-dynamic recall wall (add #18k). It is also the live candidate to un-HOLD comms-denied recovery, whose NULL was perception-availability (camera never reacquired), not guidance.
options.pros: Tracks the real pitch profile; attacks both the acquisition wall and the recovery NULL; sim-testable now (tilt-aware gt chain exists via INTERCEPTOR_SENSOR_PITCH_RAD).
options.cons: Hardware cost: servo/gimbal weight, power, actuation latency, a control loop, and a mechanical failure mode. NOT yet validated as the wall fix — and be honest about the ceiling: ADR-0070 showed availability alone does not tighten the CPA (the bearing-noise floor is insensitive to more time-in-view), so its value is acquisition/recall/handoff, not a smaller miss. [2026-07-17] REJECTED by the builder in favour of a fixed wedge (servo/gimbal complexity + power + failure mode not worth it; a fixed tilt sized to the dash pitch is good enough for the acquisition wall).

decisions.chosen_rationale: FINAL (builder 2026-07-17): the FIXED up-tilt wedge is chosen, sized to the REAL airframe's measured dash pitch (adjustable 10-30° bracket, angle from the first-dash ULog — build_plan P3; never sim-sized). Level is rejected because it leaves the acquisition-band target above the frame top during the dash (the binding wall, add #18k); adaptive tilt is rejected for simplicity (servo/gimbal weight, power, latency, failure mode — not worth it for an acquisition-first fix). The evidence arc that got here inverted twice: ADR-0070 demoted tilt (availability didn't tighten the miss), then the set-pose sweep re-promoted pointing to the #1 lever (100% static recall vs 0.8% in flight). Honest caveats stand: the prior up15 NULL (ADR-0068) was a cue-era terminal-PARITY test, not this acquisition context; a dash-pitch tilt exceeds the flush mount's ~11° clearance (forces the boom/mast geometry, bench-gated at loaded throttle); and the P0.1 frame-top off-axis sweep is the cheap falsification check that runs BEFORE any of it is bought.
decisions.evidence: ADR-0060, ADR-0065, ADR-0067 (+addendum), ADR-0068, ADR-0070, ADR-0076 add #18j-fix/#18k

decisions.question: Stay on Gazebo Harmonic + PX4 SITL, or pivot to a photoreal simulator (Isaac Sim/Pegasus, AirSim, Flightmare)?

options.name: Stay on Gazebo Harmonic + gz-transport + PX4 SITL
options.summary: Keep the existing stack, fix realism complaints in place (3D quad target, orient-to-velocity, GPU render). The adjudicated ruling.
options.why_choose: Both complaints motivating a pivot (bearing precision, unrealistic target) are algorithm/modeling issues identical in every simulator. Staying preserves the entire measured evidence base — M3 0.018–0.04 m, M4 0.945 m, the miss-vs-speed curves, Pk 72/72, ~70 ADRs — which is non-transferable to a new renderer/physics. Both realism gaps were fixed IN Gazebo for a fraction of the cost (fpv_quad_enemy + orient-to-velocity; GALLIUM_DRIVER=d3d12 GPU render, RTF 0.336 -> 0.951). A non-photoreal renderer with disclosed gaps is also MORE defensible for the sim-to-real story than a photoreal one that tempts over-claiming transfer.
options.pros: Portfolio evidence preserved; PX4+MAVSDK interface unchanged; realism fixable in place; disclosed-gap honesty.
options.cons: Not photoreal — the NN has never seen a real photon (disclosed); WSL2 render quirks (GPU-wedge, d3d12 flakiness) require operating discipline.

options.name: Pivot to Isaac Sim 5.1 + Pegasus
options.summary: The strongest photoreal candidate — preserves the PX4+MAVSDK interface via Pegasus.
options.why_choose: You would pivot if photoreal domain randomization became CENTRAL to the perception thesis: Isaac's rendering + asset ecosystem is the credible path to training pixels that transfer, and Pegasus keeps the autopilot interface.
options.pros: Photoreal pixels; banking drone assets; domain randomization tooling.
options.cons: Below this machine's hardware floor (needs >=16 GB GPU + native Linux; this box is a 4070/12 GB on WSL2); invalidates every logged number; forces a full seeker retrain on new pixels plus rebuilding every world, mover, batch harness, and gate (weeks-to-months for a solo builder). Revisit ONLY if the builder moves to native Linux + a bigger GPU AND photoreal DR becomes the thesis.

options.name: Pivot to AirSim / Flightmare
options.summary: The other surveyed photoreal/learning-oriented simulators.
options.why_choose: Only if their specific ecosystems (Unreal assets, RL tooling) were needed; the 5-agent survey found no advantage that survives the same invalidation cost.
options.pros: Unreal-grade visuals (AirSim); RL-friendly (Flightmare).
options.cons: AirSim is archived/fragmented; same evidence-invalidation and retrain costs; weaker PX4 path than Pegasus. Dominated option.

decisions.chosen_rationale: The pivot question was adjudicated by a 5-agent research workflow with an adversarial reviewer (ADR-0072): the decisive logic is that a simulator swap destroys the portfolio's entire measured evidence base to buy things (photoreal pixels, banking assets) that were obtainable in Gazebo for days not months — and the hardware floor independently rules out the best candidate. The subsequent arc vindicated it: the 3D quad + GPU render landed in-place, and the methodology that caught all five coded-dash mirages (paired seeds, control arms, gt-consistent audits) lives in this harness.
decisions.evidence: ADR-0072, ADR-0075, ADR-0076 (GPU-equivalence confirmation), project_state.json sim_harness

decisions.question: What does the target look like — the flat billboard stand-in, or a proper 3D banking quad?

options.name: Flat billboard target (fpv_target_markerless)
options.summary: Gazebo primitives laid out in a vertical plane facing -X — inherited from the AprilTag board design. The target every pre-2026-07-12 number was measured against.
options.why_choose: It was the right first target: simple, deterministic, always face-on to the approaching camera (stable detection), and its fixed aspect was originally REQUIRED to keep the AprilTag readable (ADR-0010 #6). It let the guidance arc be proven without conflating it with perception variance.
options.pros: Stable, easy detection; deterministic aspect; the substrate of the validated M0–M5 + markerless arcs.
options.cons: It FLATTERED the headline detection ~2.4x: on the same geometry, billboard 72/72 vs quad ~41% Pk (ADR-0076). It cannot bank (no bank cue possible), and orienting it just tilts a vertical wall — the 'validated banking' read was a misread the builder caught (ADR-0072 addendum #2).

options.name: 3D quad target (fpv_quad_enemy) + orient-to-velocity
options.summary: A real x500-mesh quad with a horizontal rotor plane, red enemy accents, banking into turns via the mover's coordinated-turn orientation stream (--orient-to-velocity, default-off for measured batches).
options.why_choose: Realism with integrity: a real hostile quad is seen edge-on and banking, and the honest portfolio story requires measuring against that. It also UNLOCKS the bank-as-accel cue idea (ADR-0073 — you cannot read bank off a billboard). The swap discipline was kept clean: retrain-gated, billboard retained as rollback, no measured batch confounded (orientation flag off by default).
options.pros: Honest detection difficulty; enables the bank cue; vendored mesh (clone-and-run safe); exposed the real walls the hardware will face.
options.cons: Collapsed the flattering headline (2/45 -> honest 41% baseline -> ultimately the flight-dynamic recall wall) and triggered the whole retrain/phantom/r2l investigation arc — the cost of honesty; ~25 MB of vendored mesh.

decisions.chosen_rationale: The 3D quad is chosen because the billboard's always-face-on aspect was quietly doing perception's job for it — the realistic target revealed that the project's headline detection was flattered, which is a stronger integrity story than the flattering number (ADR-0076's own framing). Every claim boundary was kept clean: old numbers stand as billboard-era results, the swap was Pk-gated, and the harness weave asymmetry found along the way (non-mirrored weave, add #12) was fixed as a fairness bug with the default-off INTERCEPTOR_WEAVE_MIRROR flag.

decisions.question: How does the interceptor reach the terminal basket — a ground-sensor-cued dash with mid-course fusion, or a coded open-loop dash with no datalink?

options.name: Ground-cued S2 architecture (stereo cue -> dash -> cue-gated handoff, --fuse-midcourse)
options.summary: The sim-era two-stage architecture: a mocked-then-real ground stereo cue guides a 16 m/s dash, hands off to the camera-only terminal via cue-validated gates. Fully built and validated through T16–T19.
options.why_choose: The case for the cue is real and measured: the running start it enables makes the whole FPV band catchable (Pk@2.5 27% -> 100%, ADR-0036), velocity emission halves the miss under a realistic degraded cue (ADR-0030), fusion rescued the markerless seeker's chronic failures 8/8 and survived the WORST-tier 2.5 m datum bias (ADR-0044), and the real stereo pipeline spine (detector -> triangulation -> live cue -> flight) works end-to-end (ADR-0052). It mirrors the parent project's sensor-to-shooter concept.
options.pros: Measured mid-course custody win; the jam-resistance STORY is testable (cue dies, camera finishes); a complete, validated evidence arc.
options.cons: The real build HAS no ground rig — the whole cue/FusedTrack/handoff-gate/coast-search machinery is absent on hardware. Worse, the adopted anti-phantom gates silently re-coupled handoff to a LIVE cue: under a mid-dash jam the deployment config FAILS CLOSED (ADR-0059 — the fix earned fail-SAFE, not recovery; 'works comms-denied' stayed HELD).

options.name: Coded open-loop dash, no datalink (--coded-dash + --dash-crossing-bias-deg)
options.summary: The real-build architecture: a pre-flight collision-lead heading (honest constant, no live data) flies an open-loop dash at 16 m/s; the camera-only terminal takes over on acquisition. ELRS is kill/arm only; nothing mid-course steers the interceptor except its own camera.
options.why_choose: Choose the coded dash because it matches the hardware that will actually exist (no rig, no link) and makes jam-resistance STRUCTURAL — there is no guidance link to jam. It was validated as an architecture A/B in sim: it beat the full cue-guided config on r2l (ADR-0076 add #18), the per-direction crossing-bias is a real open-loop aim calibration (dash ballistics land ~0.3–0.5 m CPA on line@9), and the aim tolerates up to +/-30 deg heading error while still engaging (add #18b/#18c) — an imprecise human-pointed launch works.
options.pros: Matches reality; structurally jam-proof; simpler stack; measured aim robustness; the wide ~100 deg FoV requirement flows from (and enables) the aim tolerance.
options.cons: Open-loop aim must be programmed from pre-flight target kinematics, and the bias magnitude is speed/aspect-specific (re-tune on real data). The dash ballistics are SO good they manufactured mirages — several 'sub-meter camera-guided kills' were pure unguided flybys (add #18g/#18h); every coded-dash claim now needs a dash-only control arm. And with no cue, handoff hardening against the phantom falls entirely on the camera side.

decisions.chosen_rationale: The coded dash is chosen because architecture must follow the real hardware: Fable's real-build review said to test the flight architecture before spending more perception levers, and the paired A/B showed the cue stack was not load-bearing for the intercept itself. The ground-cued arc is not wasted — it is the validated sim-era evidence base (and the ADR-0059 jam findings are exactly why removing the link is the cleaner jam story) — but everything the hardware lacks was deliberately dropped. The standing caveat is anti-mirage discipline: open-loop ballistics this good mean any camera-guidance claim needs a control arm and a gt-consistent ENGAGE audit.
decisions.evidence: ADR-0036, ADR-0030, ADR-0044, ADR-0052, ADR-0059, ADR-0076 add #18/#18b/#18c/#18e/#18g/#18h, docs/real_build_coded_dash.md

decisions.question: What compute flies the terminal seeker — Pi 5 CPU with the AprilTag baseline, Pi 5 + Hailo NPU with the markerless NN, a Pi Zero with classical CV, or a Jetson?

options.name: Pi 5 (8 GB), CPU-only, AprilTag baseline seeker for the first kills
options.summary: The staged path actually being flown first: the Pi 5's CPU runs the AprilTag detector real-time, so the first real intercepts fly the tag while the Hailo HAT stays deferred.
options.why_choose: Choose this stage because it de-risks the first hardware build: every dollar and failure mode of the NPU toolchain is deferred until a kill exists, the tag seeker is the most-validated lock in the project, and it matches the binary-kill re-scope (a tagged target drone is legitimate for the staged baseline). This is the ADR-0063 dissent's substance, kept intact inside the ratified decision.
options.pros: Cheapest, lowest-friction path to a first kill; CPU-real-time; the tag doubles as the calibration/auto-label infrastructure.
options.cons: Kills a cooperative (tagged) target only — not the markerless end-state claim; the tag is useless in a fast crossing dash (add #18e), constraining first-kill geometry to the easier straight-leg regime.

options.name: Pi 5 + Hailo-8 NPU, markerless detect-then-track stack (5–7 inch frame)
options.summary: The council-decided, builder-ratified flight compute for the markerless end-state ('B it is imperative we make markerless work'). The Hailo HAT purchase is currently DEFERRED; nothing is claimed until the Stage-0 bench measures sustained Hz/latency on the config that flies.
options.why_choose: Choose Pi5+Hailo because it is the only configuration that runs the sim-validated seeker in real time: CPU YOLO is ~5–10 FPS (measured ~13 fps YOLOv8n; the ground NN took 0.85–1.25 s/frame on a desktop CPU), which forfeits the ~14 Hz cadence the validated stack assumes against 32–58 deg/s terminal LOS rates and a ~0.41 s terminal window. Program cost beats line-item cost: flying an unvalidated cheap seeker risks the whole airframe spend.
options.pros: ~35 fps / ~29 ms end-to-end at the expected tier; runs the exact validated stack; the bench gate cuts both ways (if CPU-only sustains >=14 Hz post-soak, drop the Hailo and lighten).
options.cons: ~$70–110 + documented Hailo Dataflow Compiler friction; deployed v2 weights are Ultralytics-AGPL (Apache fallbacks pre-identified); every throughput number is vendor-tier until benched; the 5–7 inch frame class is set by the compute, not the reverse.

options.name: Pi Zero 2 W + classical frame-differencing CV
options.summary: The parent-BOM plan: ~$18, ~10 g, no ML.
options.why_choose: Only defensible on pure cost/weight — it was the original 2.5-inch build's assumption before the seeker evidence existed.
options.pros: Near-zero cost and weight.
options.cons: The board is ~20-50x short of running the validated seeker, and the algorithm is empirically dead in-repo (40/40 detections were own-airframe edges at conf 1.0). Rejected 3/3 by the council; survives only as a possible seeker-less logger.

options.name: Jetson (Orin Nano / NX) onboard
options.summary: The GPU companion computer option, twice considered.
options.why_choose: Raw TOPS headroom and CUDA — attractive if the ML path demanded it.
options.pros: Compute headroom; well-supported ML tooling.
options.cons: ADR-0012: its only real advantage for the fiducial was CUDA AprilTag via Isaac ROS, which is ROS 2 — explicitly forbidden by GOALS.md — leaving 2x price and 2–3x power for an idle GPU; and once real ML did enter, the Hailo HAT closed the gap for ~$70–110 without ROS 2 (ADR-0015). The Jetson's correct home is the GROUND node, where power/weight are free.

decisions.chosen_rationale: The compute decision is a staged pair, not a fork: Pi 5 is the board either way (council-unanimous across two eras), the AprilTag baseline flies first because it is CPU-real-time and de-risks the build, and the Hailo HAT + markerless stack is the ratified end-state gated on the Stage-0 bench (sustained end-to-end NN+tracker Hz through a thermal soak, CSRT loop time, yaw-ramp detection at terminal LOS rates). The binding principle from ADR-0063: bench the configuration that FLIES, and claim nothing until it is measured.
decisions.evidence: ADR-0012, ADR-0015, ADR-0063, hardware_order_list.md §0/§0c, project_state.json constraint pi5-compute, NEXT.md ROUND-5

decisions.question: What counts as success — a literal <1 m CPA, a proximity-Pk-vs-radius curve, a binary kill on video, or an RTK-measured sub-meter number?

options.name: Literal <1 m CPA at 9 m/s, markerless
options.summary: The original M4-derived precision bar carried forward as the real-build headline goal.
options.why_choose: It was the honest early bar: M4 legitimately passed <1 m at 2 m/s, and 'sub-meter' is a crisp, impressive resume number.
options.pros: Crisp; continuous metric; drove the early guidance rigor.
options.cons: Out of reach against a fast maneuvering target, and provably so: the pre-registered R1 rule fired (line@9 median 3.38 m, 0/12 at 1 m), the ~1.5–2 m weave CPA is the seeker floor after a four-lever elimination arc (accel-pred, t_go, tilt, subpixel — all null or worse), and hit-to-kill precision is a $M-class technique real cheap interceptors don't use (ADR-0022). Chasing it also created judging-against-the-wrong-bar errors (ADR-0021: at 2–3 m/s the intercept was ALREADY a kill).

options.name: Proximity Pk-vs-radius curve (Pk@2.5/2.8 m) — the sim metric
options.summary: Success = closest approach inside a lethal radius set by the kill mechanism's PHYSICS (ram 0.35 m (ADR-0084), net ~1.5 m, proximity ~2.5 m), reported as a full Pk-vs-R curve with CIs, per-speed, never pooled. Builder-ratified (ADR-0025); hardened to n=72 (ADR-0064).
options.why_choose: Choose the proximity metric because it is what every fielded cheap interceptor actually does (Coyote, ZIRKA/Sting, DroneHunter — all kill within a few-meter lethal/catch radius) and because the physics demands it: the miss floors kinematically ~1–2 m at speed, and you cannot buy out the perception gap with a bigger warhead (the fuze needs the same terminal detection, ADR-0021). The honesty machinery — radius fixed a priori, full curve visible, Wilson/Clopper-Pearson CIs, radius-explicit quotes only — makes the number defensible.
options.pros: Mechanism-anchored and honest; the Monte-Carlo backbone of the resume line; already earned at n=72 on the billboard-era config.
options.cons: The sim target has no collision volume, so every radius is a disclosed narrative assumption; radius-parameterized claims are easy to misquote ('95% Pk' without the radius is banned).

options.name: Binary kill (contact), confirmed on video + both ULogs — the field criterion
options.summary: The 2026-07-15 re-scope: real-world success is 'it takes the drone out or not', evidenced by seeker video + phone slow-mo + both aircraft ULogs ($0 instrumentation).
options.why_choose: Choose binary kill because it is what the builder actually wants to demonstrate, it is unambiguous on video, and it deletes an entire metrology subsystem: the RTK pair existed ONLY to measure a sub-meter CPA. Consumer GPS cannot measure <1 m anyway, so between RTK and nothing, the honest cheap criterion is contact.
options.pros: Saves $220–300 (RTK cut); unfakeable evidence; matches the kinetic-ram kill mechanism (contact IS the kill).
options.cons: No citable sub-meter number for the portfolio (RTK can be bought later solely for that); a near-miss and a miss are indistinguishable in the score, so sim Pk remains the quantitative backbone.

options.name: RTK-measured sub-meter CPA metrology
options.summary: A u-blox ZED-F9P pair to measure real CPA to sub-meter — briefly 'load-bearing, not optional' in §0b.
options.why_choose: Only if a citable real-world sub-meter NUMBER is the deliverable — it is the one way to measure a <1 m field CPA.
options.pros: Publishable precision; closes the sim-to-real measurement gap.
options.cons: $220–300 buying a measurement the re-scoped criterion no longer needs; cut in §0c. Any doc still calling RTK load-bearing is stale/superseded.

decisions.chosen_rationale: Two metrics coexist by design, each honest in its domain: the proximity Pk-vs-radius curve is the SIM metric (ratified ADR-0025 because the physics and the fielded-systems evidence both say cheap interceptors kill within a radius, not at zero), and the binary kill is the FIELD criterion (the 2026-07-15 re-scope that cut RTK). The literal <1 m headline died by pre-registered rule, not vibes — R1 fired, and the four-lever elimination arc had already shown ~1.5–2 m is the seeker floor and ALREADY a kill under the ratified metric. Teaching point: pick the bar from the kill mechanism's physics before seeing results, and never quote Pk without its radius.

decisions.question: How is the own-prop phantom (a high-confidence false detection reading ~1.5 m) kept from seeding a false handoff — appearance retrain, a range-plausibility gate, or hardware prop-clearance?

options.name: Appearance retrain / negative-mining (rebal, hardened)
options.summary: Train the detector to stop firing on the prop-arm/background phantom via mined hard negatives.
options.why_choose: The principled software fix: phantom and target are co-located in frame but differ in appearance/size, so appearance looked like the correct discriminator (position/range provably cannot separate them). The mining even achieved its literal goal — phantom suppressed, real target acquired ~13 m earlier.
options.pros: Attacks the false detection at its source; the diagnostic value was real (it proved the phantom was NOT the r2l cause).
options.cons: Every variant traded phantom suppression for real-target flight recall: rebal flew BLIND (coverage ~0, 0/16 acquisitions, its '16/16 Pk' a dash-ballistics mirage, add #18d); the hardened retrain regressed l2r to 0. The aced-frame-eval/failed-in-flight pattern, again. Closed.

options.name: Range-plausibility gates (ADR-0077 + --coded-dash-acquire-range-*)
options.summary: Reject a detection whose implied range grossly disagrees with the expected range (cue pre-handoff / r_hat post-handoff / a fixed acquisition window).
options.why_choose: The obvious cheap fix: the phantom reads ~1.5 m while the truth is 15–20 m — a 10x range disagreement looks trivially gateable, and the gate is reversible, honesty-clean, and default-off.
options.pros: Cheap, reversible, well-tested plumbing (17 unit tests); conservative bounds.
options.cons: NULL both times, for structural reasons: post-handoff a phantom seeds r_hat so the gate then rejects the TRUE closing detections — it reinforces the phantom (ADR-0077 addendum: l2r regressed 81% -> 25%); the coded-dash variant aborted BOTH directions (add #18f) — per the add #18g correction, because approach recall was ~0 (nothing real to acquire, gated or not; real and phantom ranges DO separate). Closed.

options.name: HARDWARE prop-clearance (nose-cantilever camera mount)
options.summary: Design the props out of the camera's FoV by geometry; verified by a bench corner-spin check — a HARD gate on the real build (BOM §0②). [COMMITTED 2026-07-17: builder will 3D-print the forward extension.]
options.why_choose: Choose hardware because it removes the phantom at the SOURCE: the camera-forward sim test dropped approach-phase phantom detections from 1187 to 1 (add #18h), and after ~12 software levers all returned NULL, the honest conclusion is that no software separator exists. A phantom that never renders cannot seed a handoff.
options.pros: Eliminates the false-handoff hazard structurally; verifiable on the bench before flight; no recall trade-off.
options.cons: It is NOT the acquisition fix — with the phantom gone, approach recall stayed ~0 (the wall is pointing/recall, add #18h), so expectations must stay scoped: the phantom is the false-HANDOFF hazard, not the acquisition blocker. Adds a mechanical design constraint to the airframe.

options.name: Handoff hardening (streak range-consistency + pre-flight range-plausibility window)
options.summary: Planned software belt-and-braces at the handoff decision itself, complementing the hardware fix. Unbuilt.
options.why_choose: Even with prop clearance, the 5-consecutive-detections streak is the single point where a transient false lock becomes a committed intercept; consistency checks across the streak are cheap insurance against outdoor false positives the sim never showed.
options.pros: Defense in depth at the exact commitment point; cheap.
options.cons: Only the streak range-CONSISTENCY half is genuinely unbuilt/unvalidated (and suspect — a phantom-only streak is self-consistent at ~1.5 m); the pre-flight range-plausibility window WAS built (--coded-dash-acquire-range-min/max) and NULLed (add #18f). The range-gate NULLs warn that naive range-based versions of this backfire — design against the measured failure modes.

decisions.chosen_rationale: This is the project's cleanest 'software cannot fix it' verdict: appearance retrains fail blind in flight, range gates provably reinforce the phantom, and ~12 total levers returned NULL — so prop clearance is designed in by GEOMETRY with a hard bench gate, with handoff hardening as the planned software belt. Equally important is the corrected scope from add #18g: the phantom was re-diagnosed from acquisition-blocker to false-handoff hazard, so fixing it does not buy acquisition — that lever lives in pointing/detector.
decisions.evidence: ADR-0077 (+addendum), ADR-0076 add #13/#18d/#18f/#18g/#18h, project_state.json constraint prop-clearance, hardware_order_list.md §0②

decisions.question: How is the launch aimed with no datalink — onboard acoustic tracking, a pre-flight coded collision-lead heading, or a ground acoustic launch-cue?

options.name: Onboard acoustic target tracking
options.summary: Microphones on the interceptor localizing the target by sound during flight.
options.why_choose: Attractive on paper for a no-datalink design: passive, cheap, and unjammable — a way to steer mid-course without a camera lock.
options.pros: Passive; no link; cheap sensors.
options.cons: Dead on physics: the interceptor's own props are ~40 dB louder in exactly the band that matters — the SNR is the wrong way by orders of magnitude. Ruled DEAD in the 2026-07-16 Fable strategic review.

options.name: Coded collision-lead aim (pre-flight constant, + --dash-heading-deg human override)
options.summary: The launch heading is computed once from pre-flight target kinematics (an honest constant — no live ground truth), or simply pointed by the human; the open-loop dash flies it.
options.why_choose: Choose the coded aim because the measured tolerance makes precision unnecessary: all 48 flights across the heading-error envelope still acquired/engaged at up to +/-30 deg aim error (add #18b/#18c) — an imprecise, human-pointed launch is enough, which is exactly the 'imprecise coded-dash interceptor' concept. The per-direction crossing-bias then calibrates the residual aim as a pre-flight constant.
options.pros: Zero sensors/links at launch; measured +/-30 deg robustness (enabled by the hard ~100 deg FoV requirement); dead simple.
options.cons: Requires knowing the target's rough track pre-flight (a launch-cue problem); the #18g caveat applies — read the tolerance as dash-robustness, not perception proof (ENGAGE streaks in those arms could be phantom).

options.name: Ground acoustic launch-cue
options.summary: Acoustic array on the GROUND (away from own-prop noise) detecting the inbound target and triggering/pointing the launch.
options.why_choose: The salvageable half of the acoustic idea: on the ground the SNR problem disappears, and a launch-on-detect trigger needs only coarse bearing — well within acoustic capability.
options.pros: Passive, cheap, unjammable; only needs coarse accuracy thanks to the +/-30 deg aim tolerance.
options.cons: Unbuilt, unscoped — an idea, not a design; adds a ground component to an otherwise self-contained build.

decisions.chosen_rationale: The coded pre-flight aim wins because the measured aim-error envelope (+/-30 deg) makes launch precision a non-problem — the wide-FoV camera and crossing-bias calibration absorb it. Onboard acoustics died on own-noise physics; the ground acoustic cue survives only as a future idea because it sidesteps that physics and needs only the coarse accuracy the envelope already tolerates.

decisions.question: RELEASE / LAUNCH MECHANISM: how is the interceptor deployed and the engagement triggered, and how (if at all) is a launch-time aim cue folded in without breaking jam-resistance — (A) an autonomous hand/loosely-mounted launcher that auto-fires on an NN lock, (B) a manual human-triggered coded dash, or (C) a smart launcher with a higher-res/zoom camera that transmits a live intercept cue? (Distinct from the sibling 'how is the launch AIMED' decision; this is the deployment + trigger + cue-plumbing question.)

options.name: A — Autonomous launch-on-detect from a hand/loosely-mounted perch (auto-fire)
options.summary: The interceptor sits on the launcher, camera live + NN running; the operator points it roughly at the inbound; it AUTO-LAUNCHES the instant the NN holds a lock and dashes at the detected bearing.
options.why_choose: Its real appeal: the STATIC-mounted detector works ~100% at 8-22 m (vs ~0.8% in flight), so it launches with a confirmed lock and a machine-measured bearing (~0.1 deg/px) — tighter than a human eyeball can point, and inside the ~15-20 deg kill tolerance.
options.pros: Machine-accurate launch bearing from the reliable static regime; no radio in the loop (jam-proof); the bearing-latch payload is ~$0 software.
options.cons: Dominated as a standalone: ZERO added acquisition range (same ~16 m cam) and reaction-time-starved (~1.8 s vs a 9 m/s inbound before takeoff+dash); does NOT touch the elevation/pointing wall; the pre-launch lock is unproven to survive the ~40 deg dash-pitch transient; and auto-firing a spinning-prop RAM on an unmeasured outdoor false-positive rate (ADR-0078 bird/clutter) is the least-defensible ROE. Salvageable half = the static-bearing latch, folded into B with the human keeping the fire decision.

options.name: B — Manual human-triggered launch + coded open-loop dash -> camera-only pro-nav terminal (committed baseline)
options.summary: The human sees the drone, pulls the trigger, and the interceptor dashes on a pre-flight-constant heading until the onboard camera acquires and pro-nav takes over. This IS the current committed real design (coded_dash + launch_aim stages).
options.why_choose: Cheapest (~$0), the only fully-instrumented option, jam-proof, and a human owns weapons release (most defensible ROE). Recommended EXTENSION (exploration, NOT ratified): fold in an honesty-clean launch-time aim stack — a static-camera bearing latch (A's payload) and an OPTIONAL no-radio one-shot ground spotter (C recast), both latched as SINGLE pre-flight constants; plus a $0 phone-gunsight / red-dot to hand-aim to the ram tolerance.
options.pros: No new sensor path or radio in the guidance loop; the dash aim is validated to >=30 deg acquisition tolerance; every onboard-perception fix (the fixed-tilt re-fly) is built and validated here.
options.cons: Kill-grade aim (~15-20 deg) rests on a human point unless the aim stack is added; and, like every option, the camera terminal is unproven until the fixed-tilt wedge is validated (today's kills are open-loop dash ballistics).

options.name: C — Smart launcher: higher-res/zoom camera + LIVE datalink cue (as stated)
options.summary: The launcher's better camera acquires first (farther than the drone's wide cam), computes an estimated intercept point/lead, and TRANSMITS it to the interceptor mid-course, before its own camera can see the target.
options.why_choose: The reach physics is real (R_acq linear in fx -> a zoom launcher cam could acquire at 30-65 m), and a launcher is the safe home for a narrow FOV (the ADR-0024 crosser backfire hits only the onboard terminal seeker, not a human-pointed spotter).
options.pros: Real 2-4x acquisition-range physics (sim upper bound); narrow FOV is backfire-safe on a human-pointed launcher; zero parallax at the launch instant; and the ONE-SHOT recast (no radio, latch a single pre-flight constant, link dies at launch) keeps the reach benefit while staying honesty-clean and jam-proof.
options.cons: Worst as stated: a persistent live datalink VIOLATES the no-datalink constraint (it IS the link an adversary jams — the whole jam-resistance headline), was already MEASURED to hurt aim (cue-guided r2l 0/8 vs coded-dash 5/8 @Pk2.5, from an aspect-biased bearing, ADR-0076 add #18), and re-imports the ground cue the sim deliberately mocked away. Reach numbers are pinhole UPPER BOUNDS (Stage-0-bench-gated). Survives ONLY recast as a zero-radio ONE-SHOT pre-launch spotter that latches a single pre-flight constant and lets the link die at launch — folded into B.

decisions.chosen_rationale: RECOMMENDED (design exploration 2026-07-21, NOT ratified): B-core + an honesty-clean, jam-proof launch-time aim stack — keep the committed human-triggered coded dash, and pull ONLY the pre-flight-constant pieces off A (the static-camera bearing latch) and C (an OPTIONAL no-radio one-shot ground spotter), both baked in at trigger so nothing enters the guidance loop after launch, with a mandatory link-DENIED test arm to DEMONSTRATE the camera terminal finishing unaided. Discard exactly the parts the evidence punishes: A's auto-fire (reaction-starved + unmeasured outdoor false-fire on a ram) and C's live datalink (self-refuting for the headline; measurably corrupted aim). Crucial sequencing: NO launch mechanism moves the binding wall (POINTING, owned by the still-unvalidated fixed-tilt wedge) or the real bar (0.35 m RAM (ADR-0084), not Pk@2.5 m) — so the fixed-tilt x coded-dash re-fly vs a dash-only-ballistics control is the ONE experiment that decides whether a camera terminal exists at all; build and prove that on B BEFORE buying A's or C's hardware. Higher-leverage than any launch option, left open for the builder: a 2-axis seeker gimbal (the only full elevation-decoupler, revives lock-carry), dual ONBOARD cameras (C's reach, jam-proof), or a forgiving NET kill (~1.5-2 m radius dissolves the pointing bar). BUILDER RULING 2026-07-21: RAM kill CONFIRMED (net NOT pursued for now — revisit only if the intercept proves impossible at the ram bar); the LAUNCH MECHANISM is PARKED until the first real flights show how the drone actually behaves. This recommended hybrid stands as the recommendation for when it is revisited; the active near-term effort is IMPROVING THE INTERCEPT itself (acquire earlier + hit to ram range) — see the intercept-accuracy levers program.
