decisions.question: Camera mount GEOMETRY to resolve the adaptive-tilt vs prop-clearance collision — flush-forward + tilt clamp, a longer forward boom, or an elevated centre-mast tilted up?

options.name: Flush-forward + tilt clamp (committed baseline)
options.summary: The current committed nose-cantilever (~20 mm forward), with --adaptive-tilt-max-deg clamped to the bench-verified clearance (~11° level margin).
options.why_choose: Simplest, lightest, stiffest (shortest boom = least vibration + smallest parallax). Removes the phantom for free.
options.pros: Least vibration/CG/parallax; already committed.
options.cons: Caps the up-tilt lever at the clearance angle — may be TOO LITTLE tilt to re-centre the frame-top target and recover recall (the open risk).

options.name: Longer forward boom
options.summary: Extend the overhang: moving the camera further forward pushes the props to a larger off-axis angle -> more clearance margin -> more tilt budget.
options.why_choose: Buys tilt budget by geometry if the flush clamp proves too tight, without changing the basic mount concept.
options.pros: More clearance/tilt headroom; incremental.
options.cons: Rising VIBRATION/flex at reach (attacks the very recall wall it's meant to help), forward CG shift, larger camera-CG parallax, more sacrificial material + drag. Not free — there's a sweet spot.

options.name: Elevated centre-mast, forward + tilted up (builder idea)
options.summary: A mast rising from the vehicle centre, cantilevering forward and pitched up, so the camera sits ABOVE the rotor plane and looks up-and-forward OVER the props.
options.why_choose: Geometrically the strongest: props sit BELOW the up-tilted FoV so up-tilt looks AWAY from them — it can dissolve the tilt/clearance collision AND serve the pointing wall (up-tilt re-centres the frame-top target) in ONE structure.
options.pros: Resolves the collision + helps the dominant pointing lever simultaneously; the up-tilt is 'free' clearance-wise.
options.cons: Worst structure for VIBRATION/flex (tall + forward cantilever = longest lever = most blur + extrinsic wobble, the #2 risk), raises CG (stability, top-heavy), more windage; needs a genuinely stiff/light build (carbon) to be viable.

decisions.chosen_rationale: Now DRIVEN by the fixed-tilt decision (2026-07-17): the tilt must ~= the dash pitch (~25-40°) to fix acquisition, and that FAR exceeds the flush mount's ~11° prop clearance — so the flush baseline can only deliver a partial ~10-15° tilt. A dash-pitch tilt REQUIRES the boom (longer overhang) or the elevated centre-mast (which also naturally clears an up-tilted FoV). Decide by: (1) the real airframe's measured dash pitch = the target tilt; (2) the clearance each geometry gives at that tilt (bench corner-spin across the tilt); (3) vibration-at-reach (bench modal). The elevated mast is the strongest if it can be built stiff; the flush+small-tilt is the fallback if the real dash pitch turns out small.
decisions.evidence: ADR-0076 add #18k (pointing is the dominant lever); hardware_order_list §0② (~11° level margin); Fable gap-check 2026-07-17 (tilt/clearance collision); builder mount-geometry ideas 2026-07-17.

decisions.question: INTERCEPT-ACCURACY PROGRAM: how do we improve the camera-only RAM intercept (acquire earlier + drive terminal CPA to a ~0.3-0.5 m contact) of a >=9 m/s target? (Heavy research synthesis 2026-07-21; the ranked levers below.)

options.name: Loft-then-dive + accel-capped constant-known-pitch dash, co-sized with the wedge (BIGGEST LEVER)
options.summary: Re-shape the coded dash: climb ~2-4 m early then DIVE on the co-altitude target so the 35-40 deg nose-down pitch aims the fixed camera AT the target instead of over it; cap forward accel so body pitch holds ONE bounded value (theta=arctan(a/g)) and size the wedge to exactly that pitch. Pure trajectory/own-state, honesty-clean.
options.why_choose: The ONLY lever that hits the #1 binding wall (POINTING: 0.8% in-flight detection, ~75% of 8-12 m ticks out of frame) at its geometric root; sim-cheap; and it also adds a dive g-component to Vc and shrinks t_go (tightening the ZEM budget). RECOMMENDED FIRST TEST. The wedge angle MUST be chosen jointly with the dash profile — a fixed wedge alone 'only relocates the in-view window'; loft flips the sign of the pointing error the wedge is sized against, so it must be validated BEFORE the wedge is frozen.
options.pros: Attacks the root cause; honesty-clean; recovers lost closing time via loft energy not raw tilt; every term bench-measurable from a static-thrust test.
options.cons: Sim numbers are UPPER BOUNDS (no motion-blur model); costs some peak Vc / t_go that must be netted; dive angle must not overshoot the dash pitch the other way.

options.name: FOV-holding guidance: look-angle-constrained PN + IBVS pixel-centering (Phase B)
options.summary: Add a closed-form look-angle-feedback term to the N=5 strapdown PN that refuses to drive the bearing past the usable look angle, plus an image-based visual-servoing term penalizing the target's pixel offset. Wedge = static bias; this term = the dynamic residual through the +40->-35 pitch swing. Neither differentiates a metric bearing.
options.why_choose: Makes 'keep the target in FOV' a first-class guidance constraint (extends the capturable region vs plain PN) without the noisy differentiation that sank the earlier APN/PIP attempt; microsecond cost on the Pi. Prototype on the 30 fps AprilTag baseline.
options.pros: Sim-cheap; honesty-clean (re-earns the no-cheat audit for the pixel-into-loop path); complements (does not replace) the wedge.
options.cons: BLIND if the target is already out of frame (holds a marginal target, cannot recover a lost one -> needs Phase A first); on a fixed-camera quad re-centering trades some closing authority; must be formulated against the VERTICAL pitch-coupling axis.

options.name: Terminal IMU-coast through the sub-1 m camera dropout, armed by a tau clock (Phase D)
options.summary: On the FOV-edge/track-loss flag inside ~1 m, freeze the last good LOS-rate and fly the final ~0.15 s open-loop on the own-state EKF, propagating the LOS forward; arm with a tau (time-to-contact from bbox growth) clock, NOT wall-clock. Own IMU/attitude/velocity only.
options.why_choose: Highest-confidence terminal lever and honesty-clean: the camera dies inside ~1 m on 20/20 flights and terminal LOS is 485-1870 deg/s, so a stale last command diverges fast; propagating a frozen LOS-rate preserves the commanded ZEM correction through impact. The straight-line target makes the constant-velocity extrapolation valid over the short window.
options.pros: No new guidance law; safe; validate FIRST among terminal levers so it is ready when pointing produces real tracks.
options.cons: Payoff is contingent on pointing landing first (no track to coast today); only ~2-4% of the miss (terminal window), not the headline lever.

options.name: Monocular size-based range prior fused into the Kalata R channel (Phase C)
options.summary: Compute R=fx*W/w_px from the detector bbox width (W~0.3 m known) and fuse as a coarse PRIOR into the existing alpha-beta/Kalata range channel (do not replace geometry). Sharpens t_go, which squares into the 96%-of-miss ZEM budget.
options.why_choose: Cheapest software lever, nearly free (reuses the bbox already computed), fully Gazebo-scorable, and makes the implicit W=0.3 m assumption an explicit measurement. NOT a resolution lever — extracts range from existing pixels, so it does not re-open the dead 'more pixels' debate.
options.pros: Honesty-clean; feeds the same t_go the tau clock and IMU-coast want.
options.cons: Honestly coarse (a +-1 px width error at a few-px terminal bbox is ~10% range error; W-foreshortening under bank adds noise) -> a fused prior, not a precision ranger; gated on having a detection at all.

options.name: Hardware / research escalations (gated behind Phase-A validation)
options.summary: If the cheap geometry fixes leave residual pointing/blur loss: 2-axis seeker GIMBAL (only full elevation decoupler; heavier open alternative to the wedge), DUAL onboard cameras (wide cue + narrow reach; handoff direction likely wide-near-terminal, unresolved; Pi-5 two-stream budget unbenched), event/neuromorphic camera (terminal blur-killer, bench-only), fixed motor cant (mostly redundant with the wedge). Research dark-horses: track-before-detect (temporal SNR, markerless-only), FOV-constrained RL guidance (angle-only, matches augmented-ZEM optimal), bank-as-accel APN (jink insurance only — zero on a straight-line target; feasibility-gate the bank read), IMU-motion-deblur.
options.why_choose: These are ESCALATIONS triggered only if Phase A validation shows the cheap fixes are insufficient — not first moves. The gimbal is the escalation if the residual +40->-35 pitch swing still loses the target; dual-cam/event-cam are bench/compute-gated hardware bets.
options.pros: Higher ceiling on pointing (gimbal) and reach (dual-cam) and terminal blur (event cam) than the cheap fixes.
options.cons: Cost/weight/complexity/compute on a sacrificial ~950 g Pi-5 frame; several are UNPROVEN UPPER BOUNDS and NOT Gazebo-scorable (event cam, blur) -> Stage-0 bench decides.

decisions.chosen_rationale: RESEARCH SYNTHESIS 2026-07-21 (docs/intercept_accuracy_levers.md; workflow intercept-distance-levers, 34 ideas -> 27 survived adversarial vetting, 59 sources). THE RE-FRAME: intercept-distance = terminal CPA; the RAM bar is ~0.3-0.5 m CONTACT (tighter than the Pk@2.5 m proxy). Three measured facts gate the whole program: (1) the binding wall is POINTING (target out of frame under the 35-40 deg nose-down dash; detector ~100% static 8-22 m but 0.8% in flight) -- the wedge is necessary but NOT sufficient ('a fixed tilt only relocates the in-view window'); (2) miss is ~96% ZEM-set at handoff (r^2=0.99); (3) correction capacity = 1/2*a*t_go^2 (grows with t_go SQUARED). HONEST HARD CAVEAT (ADR-0027): at 9 m/s delivered ZEM ~4 m vs ~0.27 m terminal capacity, so NO terminal-only trick makes a 9 m/s crosser sub-meter -- the win comes from getting the target IN FRAME during the dash and onto a converged collision course EARLIER with more t_go. THE PROGRAM is a causal 4-phase stack (pointing gates everything): A POINTING (loft-then-dive + accel-capped constant-pitch dash co-sized with the wedge -- the BIGGEST lever, converts ~0% camera-tracked to a live track) -> B HOLD RESIDUAL (look-angle PN + IBVS FOV-hold) -> C SHARPEN ZEM/t_go (size-based range fusion) -> D ENDGAME (terminal IMU-coast + tau). Sim has NO blur model so every acquisition/detection number is an UPPER BOUND the Stage-0 bench must confirm; first kills fly the AprilTag (some levers are markerless-only). NONE ratified -- these are ranked hypotheses each with a pre-registered sim/bench test.
decisions.evidence: docs/intercept_accuracy_levers.md (2026-07-21); workflow intercept-distance-levers (15 agents, 59 sources); ADR-0027 (ZEM r^2=0.99, t_go^2 capacity, 9 m/s ZEM-hard); ADR-0076 add #18k (pointing wall); ADR-0023/0024 (FOV backfire, LOS rates); project_state.json pointing/coded_dash/terminal

contradictions.topic: Fixed up-tilt WEDGE ANGLE: committed 'size to the full dash pitch (~25-40°)' vs the Phase A in-frame result 'keep it MODEST (~10-15°)'
contradictions.claim_a: Pointing decision (committed 2026-07-17): the fixed up-tilt wedge angle = the airframe's measured steady DASH PITCH (~25-40°, sim ~35°), to re-centre the frame-top target for acquisition.
contradictions.loc_a: project_state.json decision 'Camera pointing / adaptive tilt' (chosen: FINAL fixed wedge = dash pitch); docs/real_build_coded_dash.md
contradictions.claim_b: Phase A analytical in-frame A/B (2026-07-21): once the dash is ACCEL-CAPPED to ~20° pitch, only a MODEST wedge is needed; a wedge >=20° centres the mid-band but DUMPS the <5 m terminal target out the frame BOTTOM (the quad brakes nose-UP there). So the wedge must be ~10-15° and sized to the CAPPED pitch, not the uncapped ~35-40°.
contradictions.current_truth: Not a flat contradiction — a coupling the committed decision did not price: 'wedge = dash pitch' was premised on an UNCAPPED flat dash. Adopt the accel-cap (which caps the pitch to ~20°) and the wedge must shrink to ~10-15° or it dumps the terminal. The two levers (accel-cap + wedge) must be co-sized JOINTLY; a full-pitch-sized wedge on a capped dash is wrong.
contradictions.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-07-25 (ADR-0088): the serialized Gazebo A/B KILLED the accel cap (net-negative at correct aim: EAL 1.05 vs uncapped 0.71; framed CG 1.92 > level 1.32). With the cap dead, claim_b's premise ('wedge sized to the capped ~20° pitch') is void — the dash is LEVEL and UNCAPPED, so the wedge/up-tilt is sized to the uncapped steady dash pitch (~35-40°, from the first real dash ULog) and is gated by the boom prop-clearance (constraint forward-camera-boom), a print-time decision. See ADR-0088.

The launch aim stack is declared honesty-CLEAN because its constants are latched at-or-before the trigger: 'The AUTO leg is programmed by us, so target start/velocity are known inputs, not a live sensor read (identical status to the sim's --target-start/--target-vel).'

contradictions.claim_b: The honesty boundary polices only MID-FLIGHT reads; it has NO rule on the quality of the PRE-FLIGHT cue. C1-fallback and C2 are derived from the true target start/velocity, i.e. a cue with ZERO error — the one thing a real ground cue never has. Combined with two measured results this is load-bearing: (1) AIM is the dominant lever (correct aim alone: 1.37 -> 0.75 m, ADR-0080/0083, floor 0.71/0.43 m); (2) the 2026-07-25 re-fly showed the camera terminal does NOT beat a well-aimed open-loop dash (3/8, 1/8, 4/8 vs its dash-only twins at 0/5/15 deg aim error). If a perfect cue supplies the dominant lever and the seeker adds ~nothing on top, the seeker is decoration and the headline collapses to 'a ballistic solution to a known trajectory'.
contradictions.loc_b: docs/flight_plan_candidates.md RESULTS 2026-07-25 (re-fly table); ADR-0080/0083; project_state.json stage 'terminal' note
contradictions.current_truth: RESOLVED BY BUILDER RULING 2026-07-26: declared an explicit PROJECT CONSTRAINT (option 1 of the three recorded). The interceptor is CUED and the deliverable is the interface spec -- performance vs cue error -- not a cueing sensor. Hardware: GPS-derived cue LATCHED AT TRIGGER, link then DEAD; error injected to measure tolerance. The no-datalink constraint is preserved precisely because the cue does not survive launch. Standing consequence: zero-cue-error results are BEST-CASE UPPER BOUNDS, never the claim. Follow-on work (the cue-error sweep) is tracked, not open as a question.
